name: Direct Prompt Injection
description: An attacker crafts malicious input directly in the prompt to manipulate the LLM into performing unintended actions, bypassing instructions, or revealing system prompts.

name: Indirect Prompt Injection
description: Malicious instructions embedded in external data sources (web pages, documents, emails) are retrieved by the LLM during RAG or browsing, causing unintended behavior.

name: Training Data Poisoning
description: An adversary manipulates the training or fine-tuning data to introduce backdoors, biases, or degraded performance into the model.

name: Model Denial of Service
description: An attacker sends resource-intensive queries or high volumes of requests to exhaust model inference resources, causing service degradation or outage.

name: Sensitive Information Disclosure via Model Output
description: The model inadvertently reveals sensitive information (PII, credentials, proprietary data) that was present in training data, context window, or retrieved documents.

name: Insecure Plugin or Tool Execution
description: An AI agent or LLM invokes plugins or tools without proper authorization, input validation, or sandboxing, allowing unintended side effects or code execution.

name: Excessive Agency and Unauthorized Actions
description: An AI agent is granted overly broad permissions or autonomy, enabling it to take consequential actions (data modification, financial transactions) without adequate human oversight.

name: Model Supply Chain Compromise
description: Use of tampered, backdoored, or vulnerable pre-trained models, libraries, or dependencies from untrusted sources introduces security risks into the AI system.

name: Retrieval Augmentation Data Leakage
description: Sensitive documents indexed in a vector database are exposed to unauthorized users through the RAG pipeline due to insufficient access controls on retrieval results.

name: Embedding Inversion and Data Extraction
description: An attacker extracts or reconstructs sensitive information from vector embeddings stored in a vector database through inversion techniques.

name: Adversarial Input Evasion
description: An attacker crafts inputs specifically designed to cause the model to produce incorrect outputs, misclassifications, or bypass safety filters.

name: Model Theft and Extraction
description: An attacker systematically queries a model to reconstruct a functionally equivalent copy, stealing proprietary model weights or capabilities.
